title: BREAKFAST BITES AND BUSINESS
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is sponsoring a Social Media Workshop titled Breakfast Bites and Business Insights on Wednesday, March 25th.

This session, presented in partnership with America’s SBDC Illinois and Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Business & Industry, will focus on how to effectively use social media to benefit and grow your business. Participants will enjoy light breakfast bites while gaining valuable insights from the featured speaker, Chris Forde, Program Director of Marketing and Communications for IECC.  Participants will  learn practical tips, strategies, and tools to strengthen your online presence and better connect with your audience.

Whether you’re just getting started or looking to improve your current social media efforts, this workshop is designed to help your business shine online.  The workshop is free for Chamber Members and $5 for non members and will start at 8:30 am on Wednesday March 25th.  Space is limited RSVP today: https://forms.gle/Z46Cs5MCa1izi3ZYA

title: CHAMP CLOSES
full_story:
First Brands Group, LLC announced Monday the permanent closure of its Champion Labs facility in Albion.

In a news release, the company said as many as 1,000 employees were notified that their employment is terminated.  Because the facility is closing in its entirety, bumping rights will not apply.

The company says it regrets the decision and described the closure as permanent.

First Brands Group stated it spent several months exploring options to avoid shutting down the Albion operation.  Those efforts included seeking additional capital and actively marketing the Champion Laboratories business in hopes of finding a buyer willing to continue operations and retain the existing workforce.  Officials said announcing a potential closure earlier could have jeopardized negotiations, as interested buyers were evaluating whether they could keep the plant running.

According to the release, a serious bidder had recently advanced in the process, with both sides exchanging draft purchase agreements.  Company leaders believed they were close to reaching a deal that would have prevented the closure.

However, the sale effort ultimately collapsed.  First Brands Group said certain facilities had been relying on outside financial support to maintain operations during negotiations.  That funding was unexpectedly withdrawn before a transaction could be completed.  The loss of that support significantly reduced the company’s valuation and eliminated any remaining viable options for a sale.

In a statement, the company said that without a completed sale, it does not have access to capital markets or sufficient cash reserves to continue operating.

First Brands Group emphasized that the decision to close was made only after exhausting all alternatives and once it became clear there was no path forward, citing the sudden withdrawal of funding and changes in the sale process as unforeseen developments that forced the expedited shutdown.

title: ISA SEEKS DIRECTOR
full_story:
The Illinois Soybean Association (ISA) seeks qualified candidates to fill a vacant board seat for District 16, which includes the following counties: Clay, Richland, Lawrence, Wayne, Edwards, White and Wabash.

The ISA board is comprised of 18 district directors and six at-large directors.  Board members serve a term of three years and are eligible for three total terms.  Eligibility to serve requires candidates to be, a resident of the state of Illinois living within the district for which he or she is nominated and elected.  Of legal voting age and a producer of soybeans in Illinois subject to the assessment in the district in and for which he or she is nominated and elected, who must also have the first right of ownership in soybeans for which payment is received.

For additional information about this opportunity, please contact ISA Director of Operations, Dustin Scott, at [email protected] or 309-846-3673 for additional information or with any questions you may have.

Applications must be completed and submitted electronically no later than Tuesday, March 10th.

title: ROTARY DODGEBALL
full_story:
The Flora Rotary Club is sponsoring its 1st Annual Dodgeball Tournament on March 14th in the Conley Gym of the Flora High School.

They are looking to register teams of 10, 8 players and 2 substitutes to play in 3 co-ed divisions.  Age divisions will be 6th through 8th grade, high school students, and those 18 and over.  The tournament will start at 9 am and will cost $100 per team, or $10 per person.  Individuals who sign up will be assigned a team.  Sign up is available through a QR code on event flyers and more information is available on the Flora Rotary Facebook page.

General admission to the tournament will be $2 and each admission is registered to win a door prize.

Proceeds will be used for the pickleball courts and Flora Library Park.

title: IECC SPIN NIGHTS
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges (IECC) will host a series of Student/Parent Information Nights, known as SPIN Nights, next month to help prospective students and their families take the next step toward college enrollment.

Each campus will host its own SPIN Night from 5:30 to 7 pm on the following dates, at Frontier Community College on March 3rd, at Olney Central College on March 5th, at Lincoln Trail College on March 19th, and at Wabash Valley College at March 17th.

SPIN Night is designed as a one-stop opportunity for students and parents to explore IECC programs, connect with key staff members, and learn more about the enrollment process.

During the event, attendees can explore academic programs, speak with Financial Aid representatives, schedule advising appointments, learn about student clubs and organizations, and discover support services available through each campus’s Learning Commons.

“SPIN Night is about making college planning simple and approachable for both students and their families,” said Carrie Halbert, IECC Director of Student Engagement and Recruitment.  “We want them to walk in with questions and leave feeling confident about their next steps.”

Halbert said the event allows families to gather information in one setting rather than trying to piece together details on their own.

“Students can meet advisors, talk through financial aid options, and see the support systems we have in place,” Halbert said.  “It’s an opportunity to see firsthand how IECC helps students succeed from day one.”

Registration is encouraged.  Students and parents can scan the QR code included on promotional materials to select the campus and date they plan to attend.

In addition to SPIN Night activities, Lincoln Trail College will also host an Ag Exploration Night on March 19th, giving attendees the opportunity to learn more about agricultural programs and careers.

For more information about SPIN Nights and to register, visit iecc.edu/spin or scan the QR code on event materials.

title: SWCD SPRING FISH AND TREE SALE
full_story:
The Clay and Wayne County Soil and Water Conservation District will be holding their spring fish sale on Thursday, March 12th at 12:00 noon.  The deadline to order grass carp is tomorrow.  The deadline to order all other fish is Thursday, March 5th.

Available fish include Channel Catfish, Largemouth Bass, Hybrid Sunfish, Bluegill, Redear, Black Crappie, Fathead Minnows, and Grass Carp.

The Soil and Water Conservation District is also taking orders for its spring tree sale.  They have a nice selection of evergreens and hardwoods to choose from.  Orders will be taken until March 27th or while supplies last.  Delivery of trees will take place during the week of April 6th.

Available trees include White Pine, Blue Spruce, Norway Spruce, Red Maple, Tulip Poplar, Pecan, Red Oak and White Oak.

To place your order, please contact the Clay County Soil and Water Conservation District office at 618-508-8208 ext. 3, in Wayne County call 618-842-7602 ext. 3.

title: ILLINOIS BASIN SAFETY AWARENESS DAY
full_story:
The Illinois Petroleum Resources Board (IPRB) and Indiana Oil & Gas Association (INOGA) will be teaming up to host the Illinois Basin Safety Awareness Day tomorrow, at the 404 Seed Station in Carmi.  This event expands on the annual Illinois Basin Celebration held in Carmi since 2022, offering an extensive oilfield safety awareness-focused program in addition to the regular oilfield worker appreciation day theme.  The event will again be open to all Illinois Basin oil and gas exploration and production industry professionals, featuring a complimentary catered breakfast and lunch, as well as complimentary Illinois Basin Proud hoodies, stocking caps, flags and stickers.

The safety awareness program will kick off with a safety presentation by CountryMark Safety Manager Ben Vaupel from 10 am to10:45 am.  A team safety trivia competition led by Campbell Energy’s Alan Hatten will follow from 10:45-11:15 am.  A group drone photo will be taken outside of the 404 Seed Station from 11:15-11:30 am, followed by lunch and a live line demonstration conducted by Wayne-White Electrical Cooperative lineman and former oilfield worker Nathan Coston from 11:30 am till 12:30 pm.

Alternate time slots for Vaupel’s presentation and Hatten’s safety trivia competition will be offered from 1 pm to 1:45 pm and 1:45 pm to 2:15 pm, respectively.  Attendees will not be required to attend the afternoon sessions if they attended the morning sessions.  IPRB will also offer careers presentations and oilfield equipment demos to area high school students throughout the day, weather permitting.

Please email , text or call IPRB executive director Seth Whitehead ([email protected] or 618-367-4751) to reserve your seat today, as space will be limited.
